content.intro: Learn understanding django's project and app structure through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding Django's Project and App Structure matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines understanding django's project and app structure as part of django project structure and configuration. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Project versus application; Creating apps with startapp; Generated application files; Organizing applications by responsibility; Reusing Django applications between projects. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Project versus application
items.text: A project package holds site-wide settings and URL entry points; an app groups a reusable responsibility such as accounts or catalog. A project can install several apps.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Understanding Django's Project and App Structure
content_blocks.code:
python manage.py startapp catalog
# Add "catalog" to INSTALLED_APPS in config/settings.py
content_blocks.expected_output: Creates an app package; add it to INSTALLED_APPS before expecting app models, templates, or admin registrations to load.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
